title: Production & Cinematic Foundations
description: This tutorial series supports your transition from pre-production planning to on-set execution. The selected videos focus on essential cinematic foundations, including lighting direction, practical lighting, aspect ratios, shutter speed and motion blur, room tone, and professional set terminology. These are not optional references — they reinforce the technical and aesthetic standards required for your one-minute short film. Review them carefully before and during Production Week to strengthen your decision-making, avoid common mistakes, and work with greater confidence and efficiency on set.

children.title: 8 Steps to Cinematic Lighting | Tomorrow's Filmmakers
children.description: Master cinematic lighting in eight steps! This tutorial uses affordable equipment to demonstrate essential techniques, from shadow side shooting to adding texture with fog. Learn how lighting direction and motivated light sources dramatically impact the mood and depth of your scenes.

children.title: Roger Deakins and the Art of Practical Lighting — Cinematography Techniques Ep. 3
children.description: n this video essay, Deakins explains his approach to practical lighting and why it isn’t just about convenience, it’s about the storytelling. As the cinematographer for such gorgeously lit movies as The Shawshank Redemption, The Village, and Sicario, Deakins knows a thing or two about practical lighting.

children.title: SFX Secrets: The Power of Aspect Ratios
children.description: Uncover the cinematic power of aspect ratios. This video essay explores how filmmakers use frame size – from the
to widescreen – to enhance storytelling and evoke specific feelings. See how varying formats create unique visual experiences.

children.title: What is Shutter Speed — Camera Shutter and the Exposure Triangle Explained
children.description: In this cinematography and photography tutorial, we will continue our Exposure Triangle series with a look at the pivotal role of the camera shutter. Included are topics on shutter speed, the difference between shutter angle vs shutter speed, motion blur, and how all of the effects of these settings are wanted or unwanted depending on your vision.

children.title: What is room tone and why you should use it in 2 minutes (How to use room tone tutorial)
children.description: In film and video production, the term room tone means the sound of an empty room, or a room in which all the actors are standing silently.

children.title: Top 50 Film Set Lingo You Should Know
children.description: Ever wonder about all that lingo they use on a film set, and what it really means?  In this video, I go through the essential 50 slang words that film crews will use on a real set.  Study these and you'll be ahead of the gang on your first day on the job!  Or, maybe it just comes in handy on trivia night.
